prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
We have selected a loss estimation methodology, utilizing a third-party model. See also Notes 1 and 3 to the unaudited consolidated financial statements for further discussion of our adoption of ASU 2016-13.

Allowance for Credit Losses - Loans. We maintain an allowance for credit losses to absorb probable and inherent losses in our loan portfolio. The allowance is based on ongoing quarterly assessments of the estimated lifetime losses in our loan portfolio. In evaluating the level of the allowance for credit losses, we consider the types of loans and the amount of loans in our loan portfolio, historical loss experience, adverse situations that may affect the borrower’s ability to repay, the estimated value of any underlying collateral, prevailing economic conditions, and other relevant factors determined by management. We follow all applicable regulatory guidance, including the “Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit losses,” issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Department of the Treasury, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and National Credit Union Administration. We believe that the Bank’s Allowance for Credit Losses Policy conforms to all applicable regulatory requirements.

nonint.text: Non-interest expense decreased $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $11.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to lower compensation costs due to lower incentive compensation and lower data processing costs, partially offset by higher loan workout expenses in other expenses.

nonop.text: Non-interest expense decreased $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $11.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to lower compensation costs due to lower incentive compensation and lower data processing costs, partially offset by higher loan workout expenses in other expenses.

tax.text: Provision for income taxes decreased by $0.2 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, largely due to a lower effective tax rate.

net.text: We reported net income of $5.4 million and $10.3 million, or $0.56 and $1.06 per diluted share for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $3.7 million and $10.1 million, or $0.37 and $1.02 per diluted share for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively.

Net interest income.text: Compared to the third quarter of 2025, the third quarter of 2026 net interest income increased $1.3 million. The third quarter 2026 increase from the same period in 2025 was largely due to an increase in average loan balances and lower interest-bearing liabilities costs, with the impact of higher average deposit balances, largely offset by higher interest-bearing cash.

intro.text: Citizens Community Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) is a Maryland corporation organized in 2004. The Company is a bank holding company and is subject to regulation by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (“OCC”) and by the Federal Reserve Bank. Our primary activities consist of holding the stock of our wholly-owned subsidiary bank, Citizens Community Federal N.A. (the “Bank”), and providing commercial, agricultural and consumer banking activities through the Bank. At December 31, 2025, we had approximately $1.782 billion in total assets, $1.524 billion in deposits, and $187.9 million in equity.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
